literal_meaning: বড় (big) + হাজারি (from 'bazaar' or market, implying substantial or full)
figurative_meaning_bn: ভারতে আগত সাহেবদের ভাষায় মধ্যাহ্নের ভরপেট আহার
figurative_meaning_en: In the parlance of the British who came to India, a hearty midday meal
example_sentences_in_bangla: অফিস থেকে ফিরে বড়হাজারি খাওয়া হবে।
সাহেবরা সকালে হালকা খেয়ে দুপুরে বড়হাজারি করত।
example_sentences_in_english: We'll have a big lunch after returning from the office.
The British used to have a light breakfast and a hearty lunch in the afternoon.
history: Originating from the Anglo-Indian colonial period in British India, where 'bara bazar' or similar terms referred to the main midday meal eaten by Europeans, reflecting the fusion of British customs with local contexts.
note: This idiom preserves a slice of colonial linguistic heritage in Bengali, now largely archaic.
